ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle DEF, D is at the lower left, F is at the lower right, and E is above. Point S is located on DE, point T is located on EF, and point U is located on DF; the three line segments from D to T, from E to U, and from F to S intersect at point A. On line segment EU, EA is labeled y, and AU is labeled 2.9. Reasoning: The problem gives that S, T, U are respectively the midpoints of DE, EF, DF, so DT, EU, FS are all medians of triangle DEF, and they intersect at the centroid A of the triangle. The centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio from the vertex to the midpoint. Therefore on median EU, EA:AU = 2:1. Given AU = 2.9, so EA = 2 × 2.9 = 5.8. Since EA = y, y = 5.8.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: triangle DEF has midpoints S on DE, T on EF, and U on DF, and the three drawn segments DT, EU, and SF meet at point A. On median EU, the diagram labels AU = 2.9 and EA = y. From the text, use that S, T, and U are midpoints, so DT, EU, and SF are medians of triangle DEF. Apply the centroid theorem: the medians meet at centroid A, which divides each median in a 2:1 ratio measured from the vertex to the midpoint. Therefore on median EU, EA = 2·AU = 2·2.9 = 5.8, so y = 5.8.
